summary: Iteration 6 full retest (backend + frontend). Backend: 100 pytest tests run, 99 pass / 1 fail (billing portal 500). New suite /app/backend/tests/test_iteration6_stripe_wizard_bulk.py (39 tests) covers Stripe reconnect, checkout without tax, signed-webhook upgrade/downgrade, register-wizard payload, strict Pydantic validations and POST /api/workers/bulk. Verified the Stripe keys belong to acct_1NfUSOEElIPXa4JR (standard, FR, charges_enabled), lookup_key shiftflow_pro_monthly -> price 4900 EUR/month under prod_V6sLUSy2g9m7Ga, checkout session has automatic_tax disabled, amount_tax=0 and custom_text.submit='TVA non applicable, art. 293 B du CGI' (visible on the real Checkout page, NO 'Unclaimed' badge). Frontend: register wizard works end-to-end on a brand new account (3 QCM + pain + form, Next disabled until answered, exactly ONE POST /api/auth/register with onboarding_answers, straight redirect to /app/dashboard, onboarding_completed=true, no /onboarding hop). UpgradeModal verified on all four 402 paths (mission create, mission duplicate, worker add, bulk quota) with CTA href=/pricing and working close. nav-upgrade-cta visible for free / absent for pro. Mission rows clickable with duplicate stopPropagation OK. Bulk import preview + creation OK (3 valid rows -> 3 created; 8 rows at free limit -> 6 created / 2 skipped -> quota_hit modal). Regression OK: login (httpOnly cookie, $2b$ hash), dashboard banners, calendrier, historique, settings (subscription block, upgrade link free / portal btn pro -> billing.stripe.com), test SMS (Twilio TRIAL blocked message), public /m/{token}, multi-shift mission creation, /payment/success 'Bienvenue en Pro !'.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Server Error (unhandled stripe.InvalidRequestError: "No such customer: 'cus_V6pJBuEk7xFA69'"). The admin still carries a stripe_customer_id created on the PREVIOUS Stripe sandbox; after the account switch that customer does not exist on acct_1NfUSOEElIPXa4JR. Two fixes needed: (a) wrap billing_portal.Session.create in try/except stripe error -> 400/409 with a French message, (b) clear/migrate stale stripe_customer_id values. Verified the endpoint works (redirects to https://billing.stripe.com/p/session) once the user has a customer that exists on the new account.

The worker sees 'Lien invalide' only by accident (frontend catch-all).

lookup_key 'shiftflow_pro_yearly' no longer exists on the new product -> 400 'Prix inconnu'. No user impact today (/pricing only offers monthly) but create the yearly price if the annual plan is still planned.
Still unauthenticated and still upgrades the user referenced in the session metadata (carried over from iteration 5, unfixed).
Still no brute-force lockout after 5 failed attempts (auth playbook item, unfixed).

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid=wf-err-email is UNREACHABLE. The email field is <input type="email"> and the other fields are required, so the browser's native constraint validation fires on submit (English tooltip "Please include an '@' in the email address") and preventDefault-blocks the handler, so validateWorker() never runs and no French inline error is shown. With a syntactically valid email the custom errors (wf-err-first / wf-err-last / wf-err-phone) do render correctly. Fix: add noValidate to the <form> (and/or type="text" inputMode="email") so the custom French validation always wins.
<Toaster /> is rendered twice (lines 41 and 43) -> risk of duplicated toasts. Remove one.

integration_issues.issue: NOT verifiable by automation: Stripe Checkout serves an anti-bot challenge to Playwright (page body contains 'I am an AI agent acting on behalf of someone else') and the 'Card' payment-method radio never becomes clickable, so the payment cannot be submitted headlessly. Covered indirectly: a real session was created, and a HMAC-signed checkout.session.completed webhook (real whsec_ secret) was accepted (200) and produced plan=pro / subscription_status=active / stripe_customer_id set / tx payment_status=paid, and customer.subscription.deleted downgraded back to free/canceled. A HUMAN must do one manual 4242 payment to confirm the transaction lands in the acct_1NfUSOEElIPXa4JR test dashboard.

issues: Merchant name displayed is 'Guyguy' with a 'Sandbox' badge instead of 'ShiftFlow' — set the public business/display name in Stripe settings (the previous 'Unclaimed sandbox' badge is gone, and price/TVA notice render correctly).
Progress bar renders ~84% instead of 100% on the 'Finalisation' step at the moment it mounts (CSS transition timing); header correctly reads 'Étape 5/5'. Cosmetic only.

critical_code_review_comments: Every stripe_lib call in server.py except payment_status_endpoint is unguarded; create_checkout and billing_portal will 500 on any StripeError. Wrap them and return 4xx with the Stripe message.

POST /api/workers/bulk silently drops duplicate-phone rows: they are counted neither in created nor in skipped_quota, so the UI toast ('N ajoutés') under-reports without explaining why. Return a skipped_duplicate count.

Validation regexes (NAME_RE / PHONE_DIGITS_RE / EMAIL_RE) are duplicated verbatim in server.py WorkerIn and Workers.js — acceptable but they must be kept in sync; note the name regex rejects digits AND underscores (broke older tests using 'TEST_Free').
server.py is still 1412 lines mixing auth/SMS/missions/cron/Stripe; check_quota_or_raise and _get_plan are still forward-referenced with '# noqa: F821'.
Most user docs have no 'plan' field at all (only 3/8 do); _get_plan defaults to free so behaviour is fine, but a backfill would make quota debugging deterministic.

rca_of_the_issue: Portal 500: switching the Stripe keys to acct_1NfUSOEElIPXa4JR invalidated every stripe_customer_id previously stored in Mongo (they belonged to the old sandbox). billing_portal.Session.create raises stripe.InvalidRequestError 'No such customer', which is not caught, so FastAPI returns 500 (backend.err.log lines ~1655-1795). Repro: login as admin -> /app/settings -> flip plan to pro -> click settings-portal-btn. Mitigation: catch StripeError -> 400 'Aucun abonnement actif' + unset the stale customer id (or re-resolve it by email via stripe.Customer.list). Public-mission 500: the token belongs to a mission_worker document created before the shifts refactor, so slot['shift_id'] raises KeyError instead of falling through to the 404 branch.
